en.headline: Industry says new renovation council will draw legitimate contractors back
en.dek: Representatives from the renovation sector said the Building Maintenance Support and Services Council’s integrity checks would help restore order and encourage qualified firms to return to the market.
body: Industry representatives said on Monday that the new Building Maintenance Support and Services Council, headed by Financial Secretary Paul Chan, would help draw legitimate consultants and contractors back into the building maintenance market.

Kenny Tse Chi-kin, vice-president of the Hong Kong Institute of Surveyors, said the council’s scrutiny of the tendering process, including background checks by law enforcement, would sustainably restore order and attract more qualified firms over time.
The non-statutory body is expected to be established by the end of the year and will take over, in phases, building-upkeep subsidy schemes previously run by the Urban Renewal Authority.
The council forms part of the government’s regulatory overhaul announced after the independent committee’s report on the deadly Tai Po fire last November.

zh.headline: 業界指新維修監察機構有助吸引合規承辦商重返市場
zh.dek: 裝修業界代表表示，樓宇維修支援及服務委員會的誠信審查將有助恢復市場秩序，鼓勵合資格公司重新參與。
body: 業界代表周一表示，由財政司司長陳茂波領導的新樓宇維修支援及服務委員會，將有助吸引合規的顧問及承辦商重新進入樓宇維修市場。
香港測量師學會副會長謝志堅表示，委員會對招標程序的審查，包括執法部門的背景檢查，將可持續恢復秩序，並長遠吸引更多合資格公司。
這個非法定機構預計年底前成立，並將分階段接管市建局目前運作的樓宇維修資助計劃。
委員會是政府在獨立調查委員會就去年大埔致命火災報告後公布的監管改革一部分。
